newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino Land shares fall on cash call fear.
newsitem.headline: Sino Land shares fall on cash call fear.

text.p: Shares of Sino Land Co Ltd fell on Wednesday morning on fears of a possible cash call after the company bought a site at a government land auction at a record price, brokers said.
The shares fell HK$0.20 to HK$8.25 in mid-morning on volume of 1.28 million shares worth HK$10.59 million.
"I think the site was a bit expensive and that triggered a cash call fear," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
Brokers said concerns of possible cash calls in the longer term to raise funds for the development of the site also triggered selling.

A consortium equally-owned by Sino Land and its chairman Robert Ng's family purchased a site in Chai Wan at a Hong Kong government land aution on Tuesday for HK$11.82 billion, a record price for government land auctions.
Ng told reporters on Tuesday that total investment for the development would be about HK$20 billion.
